current_content_summary: Provides programmable/lazy random-oracle constructions, parameterized (abstract theory FullRO) by an input type in_t, output type out_t, and sampling operator dout : in_t -> out_t distr. Defines module type RO (init/get/set/rem/sample) and RO_Distinguisher; module MkRO.RO is the standard LAZY random oracle backed by an (in_t, out_t) fmap, with LRO an alias exposing the same interface but a no-op sample. A richer module type FRO tracks each query with a Known/Unknown flag (type flag) via an (in_t, out_t * flag) fmap, adding queried/allKnown procedures -- with RO_FRO_init/get/set/rem/sample/D equivs proving FRO is equivalent to the plain RO once flags are erased (noflags). A `Collision` section proves fcoll_bound, a birthday-style collision-probability bound using the fel tactic, parameterized by a target function f, a per-collision probability bound Pc, and a query-count bound q. The `FullEager` theory (needs `dout_ll`, i.e. dout lossless everywhere) defines RRO, an 'eager-resampling' wrapper around FRO with a resample procedure (backed by IterProc), and proves eager_init/get/set/rem/sample/queried/allKnown -- the standard lazy<->eager sampling swap lemmas -- culminating in an Eager module and an Eager_1_2 equiv connecting a distinguisher run against the lazy FRO to one run against RRO with resampling. `FinEager` (needing in_t to be a FinType) adds FinRO, which eagerly pre-samples the ENTIRE domain at init via a while-loop over FinFrom.enum, and proves it equivalent to the plain RO. Finally FunRO gives a fully MONOLITHIC alternative: it samples one function in_t -> out_t all at once via `dfun dout` at init, rather than maintaining a map lazily at all -- with equivalence proofs to FinRO via DJoin.JoinMapSampling.
requires: AllCore, FMap, Distr, Mu_mem, FinType, StdBigop, FelTactic; (FullEager also pulls in List, FSet, IterProc; FinEager pulls in List and clones FinType/MUniFinFun/DJoin).
import_repair_note: PROM depends directly on FMap (not just SmtMap), so the r2025.02 SmtMap split is relevant transitively: PROM's RO.m / FRO.m fields are FMap.fmap-typed, and any proof reasoning about them (e.g. via dom/rem/eq_except) is really reasoning about FMap's current API.
version_diffs_found: No PR title in the scanned changelog window names 'PROM' directly, but PROM interacts closely with two things that DID change: the r2026.02 'new lazy/eager logic' (#787) and the r2026.07 'stronger precondition in pRHL tactics eager-seq and eager-while' (#1059) -- both are exactly the eager/lazy-sampling machinery PROM's FullEager theory relies on, so PROM proofs written against pre-r2026.02/r2026.07 EasyCrypt versions are a reasonable place to look first if an eager-related proof breaks on upgrade.
